bss.topic: Lateralidade: direita, esquerda, frente e atrás

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Com qual mão a maioria das pessoas escreve?
questions.hint: Pense em quem você conhece: qual mão é mais usada?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Levante a mão direita. Seu coração fica mais perto de qual lado do peito?
questions.hint: Coloque a mão no peito e sinta o batimento.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que fica na FRENTE do seu corpo?
questions.hint: A frente é o lado para onde você olha.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que fica ATRÁS do seu corpo?
questions.hint: Atrás é o lado que você não consegue ver sem um espelho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Complete: o contrário de direita é ___.
questions.hint: É o outro lado do seu corpo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Complete: o contrário de frente é ___.
questions.hint: Pense nas suas costas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Lia está na fila. Rafa está logo atrás dela. Quem está na frente?
questions.hint: Quem está atrás vê as costas de quem está na frente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na mesa, o copo está à direita do prato. Onde está o prato em relação ao copo?
questions.hint: Se um está à direita, o outro fica do lado oposto.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Tomás está de frente para você e levanta a mão direita dele. Para você, essa mão aparece de que lado?
questions.hint: Quando alguém está de frente, os lados ficam trocados para quem olha.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Você está olhando para a lousa. O que fica atrás de você?
options: a porta do fundo da sala
a mesa da professora, bem na sua frente
questions.answer: a porta do fundo da sala
questions.hint: A lousa está na frente; o fundo da sala fica do outro lado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase descreve a posição certa? Uma bola está entre você e a parede, e você olha para a parede.
options: A bola está na sua frente.
A bola está atrás de você.
A bola está em cima de você.
questions.answer: A bola está na sua frente.
questions.hint: Você olha para a parede, e a bola está no caminho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na fila há Bia, depois Leo, depois Duda. Quem está atrás de Leo?
questions.hint: Siga a ordem da fila.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Para virar para trás, você precisa…
questions.hint: Quem olha para trás vira o corpo todo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Você entra numa sala e a janela está à sua direita. Você dá meia-volta. Agora a janela fica de que lado?
questions.hint: Ao dar meia-volta, direita e esquerda trocam.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique como você sabe qual é a sua mão direita.
questions.hint: Pense numa coisa que você faz sempre com uma das mãos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Descreva onde está um objeto da sua sala usando as palavras direita, esquerda, frente ou atrás.
questions.hint: Escolha um objeto e diga em relação a você ou a outra coisa.

en.topic: Present and past tense, including progressive

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a verb in the past tense?
questions.hint: Past tense tells us it already happened.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is in the present tense?
options: I was playing in the park.
questions.hint: Present tense is happening now or usually.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write the past tense of 'walk'.
questions.hint: Many past tense verbs end in -ed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write the past tense of 'go'.
questions.hint: This verb does not use -ed.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Yesterday, Mia ___ a cake.
questions.hint: The word 'yesterday' is a clue.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Right now, the dog ___ in the garden.
questions.hint: 'Right now' means it is happening at this moment.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the past progressive form?
questions.hint: Look for 'was' or 'were' and an -ing verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: We ___ swimming when it started to rain.
questions.hint: The rain started in the past.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write the -ing form of 'sing' to finish: The birds are ___.
questions.hint: Add -ing to the end of the verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the present progressive form?
questions.hint: Look for 'is', 'am' or 'are' and an -ing verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence has a mistake with the tense?
options: Last week I go to the zoo.
Last week I went to the zoo.
Every week I go to the zoo.
questions.answer: Last week I go to the zoo.
questions.hint: Does 'last week' match the verb?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Change this sentence to the past tense: I eat an apple.
questions.hint: 'Eat' does not use -ed in the past.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the correct word: Ben ___ his teeth every morning.
questions.hint: 'Every morning' means something that happens usually.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the verb that keeps the tense the same: Zara opened the box and ___ a puppy.
questions.hint: The first verb is in the past tense.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one sentence about what you did last weekend. Use a past tense verb.
questions.hint: Start with 'Last weekend I…'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one sentence about what someone in your house is doing right now. Use 'is' and an -ing verb.
questions.hint: For example, think about a pet or a grown-up.

en_read.topic: Funny stories: The Twits — characters through their actions

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a story, how can we find out what a character is like?
options: by looking at what they do and say
by looking at the cover only
questions.answer: by looking at what they do and say
questions.hint: Actions are clues.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'infer' mean when we read?
questions.hint: The story does not always tell us straight away.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Mr Grumble hides a frog in his wife's bed. What can we infer about him?
questions.hint: Think about why someone would do this.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Mrs Snort puts glue on the bird table so the birds get stuck. What is she like?
questions.hint: Would a kind person do this to birds?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A man never washes his beard and keeps old food in it. Which word describes him best?
questions.hint: Think about food stuck in a beard.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which of these is a funny made-up word?
questions.hint: It is not a real word you would find in a dictionary.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do authors use silly words in funny stories?
questions.hint: Think about how silly words make you feel.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Some monkeys are made to stand on their heads all day. They work together to escape. What can we infer about the monkeys?
questions.hint: Escaping together takes good ideas and courage.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence tells us what a character DOES?
options: Granny Pip shared her sweets with everyone.
questions.answer: Granny Pip shared her sweets with everyone.
questions.hint: Look for an action word.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Granny Pip shared her sweets with everyone. What does this action tell us?
questions.hint: Sharing is a clue about her heart.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A character plays a trick, but the trick goes wrong and he ends up stuck upside down. Why is this funny?
options: The trick turns back on the trickster.
questions.answer: The trick turns back on the trickster.
questions.hint: Who wanted to trick someone, and what happened to him?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Two characters keep playing tricks on each other to make each other miserable. Which word describes them best?
questions.hint: Would you want them as friends?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word is a funny sound word?
questions.hint: Say it out loud. Does it sound like a noise?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A boy shouts 'Ha! Got you!' after hiding his sister's shoes. What does this show?
questions.hint: Think about how he feels when he says 'Ha!'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Think of a character from a funny story you know. What do they do that shows what they are like?
questions.hint: Name one action and say what it shows.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do you think readers enjoy stories about nasty characters who get what they deserve?
questions.hint: Think about how it feels when a trick backfires.

en_spell.topic: Doubling the consonant before a suffix

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.hint: 'Pat' has one short vowel and ends in one consonant.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -ing to 'drop' and write the whole word.
questions.hint: Short vowel + one consonant: double it.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -ed to 'pat' and write the whole word.
questions.hint: Double the t.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -er to 'sad' and write the whole word.
questions.hint: Double the d.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -est to 'sad' and write the whole word.
questions.hint: Double the last consonant first.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -er to 'run' to make a word for a person who runs. Write the whole word.
questions.hint: Double the n.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Add -y to 'run' and write the whole word.
questions.hint: Double the n before adding y.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: hu_ _ing
questions.hint: The same letter goes in both gaps.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: dro_ _ed
questions.hint: The same letter goes in both gaps.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Why do we double the 't' in 'patted'?
options: 'pat' has a short vowel before one consonant
questions.answer: 'pat' has a short vowel before one consonant
questions.hint: Say 'pat' slowly and listen to the a.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word does NOT double its last letter when you add -ing?
questions.hint: Look at how many consonants are at the end.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Choose the correct spelling: The baby was ___ a tune.
questions.hint: Hum + -ing.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Choose the correct spelling: My nose is ___ today.
questions.hint: Run + -y.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: runing → running; droped → dropped; sader → sadder; huming → humming; runer → runner
questions.text: Yesterday I was runing in the park when I droped my ice cream. I felt sader than ever. A kind lady patted my head while her dog was huming along. She said I was the best runer she had seen, so I smiled and felt much better.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which spelling of 'hum' + -ed is correct?
questions.hint: Double the last letter before adding -ed.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words in the story about Tom.
questions.answer: droping → dropping; pating → patting; sadest → saddest; runer → runner; runy → runny
questions.text: Tom was droping his toys on the floor. His cat was pating them with her paw. Mum hummed a song and said it was the sadest mess she had ever seen. Tom was the fastest runer in the house, so he tidied up quickly while the jelly went a bit runy on the table.
